name: orbiton
description: Fast and config-free text editor and IDE limited by VT100

repo.name: orbiton
repo.description: Snappy and configuration-free little text editor/IDE for the terminal. Suitable for writing git commit messages, editing Markdown, config files, source code, man pages and for quick edit-format-compile cycles when programming. Has syntax highlighting, jump-to-error, rainbow parentheses, macros, cut/paste portals and a simple gdb front-end.

readme.summary: Well-structured README that clearly conveys the editor's purpose and unique features, but lacks troubleshooting guidance and configuration details beyond themes.
readme.top_issue: No troubleshooting section — common issues like terminal compatibility, missing dependencies, or key binding conflicts are not addressed anywhere.

injection_risks.description: No eval(), exec() or SQL string concatenation found, but os.Chmod() and os.Remove() are used with user-controlled input.
The 'bat' command is executed with user-controlled input, potentially allowing for command injection attacks if not properly sanitized.

critical_findings: Potential command injection vulnerability with the 'bat' command.
Lack of input validation for filename arguments and clipboard data.
security.summary: The Orbiton package has some security concerns, including potential command injection vulnerabilities and lack of input validation, but no critical secrets or error exposure issues were found.

common_complaints: Build failures in releases (v2.65.7, v2.68.0 panic)
stdin/pager functionality broken (MANPAGER, reading from stdin)
sentiment.summary: Orbiton shows active maintenance with responsive issue closure, but recurring stability bugs and unresolved long-standing feature requests (Windows support since 2020) indicate moderate community health with user frustration around reliability.

communication.summary: The maintainer's responses are clear, helpful, and patient. They provide technical depth and encourage new contributors.

concerns: No commits in the past 6 months despite claiming last commit today (data inconsistency)
No active contributors in past 6 months
Extended dormancy period before possible recent activity
positive_signals: No open issues indicates clean state
maintenance.summary: Project shows staling with 6 months of inactivity despite a recent commit, suggesting sporadic maintenance rather than active development.
